The parent account is therefore updated to record the tested voter counts and to drop the three-voter limitation. To finish the persistence question the same way, the driver is now also run for ten seconds, which a local construction run shows keeps the follower at its snapshot index while the frontier advances from 83 to 123 and one stable leader set holds throughout; that receipt is requested here.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: a follower that accepts an InstallSnapshot whose index does not exceed its own cached last log index keeps advertising a log it no longer holds, fails every prev-log check from that leader and accepts no further log entry, while the leader retries the same snapshot; the starvation ends only when a snapshot above the cached claim is published, and it reproduces at three and five voters. Source basis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (src_install_snapshot_tail); getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry, state.go 160-174); the non-monotonic compaction path keeps any suffix above the snapshot index while the monotonic branch deletes the whole store without resetting the claim (src_compaction, snapshot.go 217-279); prev-log verification then misses below the store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix (src_append_prev_check, raft.go 1458-1606); the leader walks nextIndex down one step per rejection (src_replicate_failure, replication.go 240-300) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, which jumps to SEND_SNAP and, on acceptance, resets nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1 (src_send_snapshot_result, replication.go 352-372). Decided evidence: the settled comparison set (execution b6089b103bbb467199d051f4492e82c8, trimmed probe index 14) with the untrimmed control negative on the same fields (index 29); the monotonic-store variant, where the store was emptied while the claim persisted (execution 20c7c72772474093bd6093a37b84448f, probe index 14); the repair boundary, where driving the leader past the claim of 97 and publishing a snapshot at 98 restored the follower to the frontier (same receipt, probe index 33); and the five-voter repetition (execution 14e86faf6ccc4b13af3ee46c65cc08dc, setup index 0 and probe index 14), where the premise recorded a claim at index 102 in term 2 over a snapshot at 83 in term 3 and the probe again showed repeated installs, the follower's applied index fixed while the frontier advanced, and the claim persisting with its suffix kept. Limits: measured on InmemStore plus FileSnapshotStore and its in-process monotonic wrapper with TrailingLogs=10 against a large control, an idle cluster with one write per 250 ms sample, 3-4 s windows and one induced partition, now repeated at three and five voters; a ten-second persistence run is requested with this update and is currently construction feedback (follower fixed at 83 while the frontier reached 123, restores 5 -> 4883, one stable leader set); the vote-decision consequence of the claim is decided in the child question, the configuration-change and wedge consequences likewise, and the follower's commit index staying 0 through the install path is reported as an advertised-state inconsistency rather than an independent defect.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control accepted no snapshot, repaired the stale suffix with entries and reached the frontier in every run, so a stale suffix alone does not stall replication.
A successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower never campaigned: every receipt shows one stable leader set with the follower's term fixed.

The starvation is bounded: with a snapshot published above the claim (97 -> 98) the follower caught up to the frontier, so the claim is starvation while the newest snapshot index stays at or below the claim.
The monotonic-store case stalls with an empty log store, so a surviving on-disk suffix is not required for the defect.
limitations: Store and snapshot implementations are the in-process ones (InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, the monotonic wrapper); a production BoltDB-style store is not available in the captured package.
Windows measured are 3-4 s, with a ten-second persistence run requested here; the frontier advance during a window is bounded by the one write per sample.

The configuration-change and vote consequences are decided in the child question and are not re-measured here; the child's minority bound assumes no configuration change between the orphaned suffix and the snapshot install.

scope.description: Two new cases of the same three-voter history, each built on the unchanged scenario (isolated leader appends entries that never reach a quorum, is shut down, remaining voters elect a leader, commit further entries and take a snapshot, isolated node restarted on its real log store and reconnected). basis.prefix: Same scenario driver as the earlier revisions, now parameterised by log-store monotonicity and by an optional repair step. Case one: the trimmed history runs with MonotonicLogs=true; the follower's install deletes its entire log store, and the probe reports whether installs repeat, whether the follower reaches the frontier, whether the cached claim persists, and whether any suffix above the snapshot index survived in the store. interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: in this revision, a follower that accepts a snapshot while its own cached log extends at or beyond the leader's snapshot index is left with an inconsistent log claim and never accepts another log entry from that leader. Basis: installSnapshot updates lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (raft.go 1930-1977), while getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (state.go 160-175). Compaction cannot remove the stale suffix in the non-monotonic store path when TrailingLogs exceeds the log length (snapshot.go 217-252), so the follower's store keeps entries above the snapshot index whose terms differ from the leader's; every AppendEntries prev-log check then either misses below the store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix, the leader's nextIndex is only decremented one step per rejection (replication.go 247-252) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, and the leader responds by re-shipping the same snapshot (replication.go 296-300, 352-372). Restricted to the measured conditions: three voters, in-memory store, FileSnapshotStore, TrailingLogs=10, an idle cluster plus steady new writes, and a follower restarted on its real on-disk log whose orphan suffix (indexes beyond the leader's snapshot index, lower term) is preserved. Local construction feedback for the same harness (native feedback only, not a retained receipt) showed the follower's FSM restored 4 -> 1365 times in a 3s window while the leader's snapshot index stayed at 83, the follower's applied index stayed at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95, the follower's cached last log claim stayed (98, term 2) against snapshot (83, term 3), its commit index stayed 0, and its store kept indexes 84-98; the untrimmed control on the identical history accepted no snapshot, repaired the suffix with entries and caught up (applied 83 -> 95). Counterevidence considered: the concern that the follower's own election timeout would repair the situation is not observed, because a successful InstallSnapshot refreshes lastContact, so no spurious election fires; and the control refutes 'any stale suffix stalls replication'. Limits: the formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained run of the requested experiment; the reachability of the trigger in production depends on a voter whose log suffix is both longer than the leader's snapshot index and stale in term (a deposed leader or a follower that stored entries from a superseded leader) together with log trimming on the leader; monotonic-store deployments delete the stale suffix instead of keeping it, so their failure mode (entry starvation with the leader's snapshot index at or below the cached claim) still needs its own receipt.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control with the same history repaired the stale suffix using log entries alone, so a stale suffix by itself is not sufficient; the install-snapshot path with a trimmed leader log is the trigger.
The successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower does not force an election and the starved state is stable rather than transient in the measured configuration.
limitations: The measured configuration used in-memory stores plus a file snapshot store, TrailingLogs=10, three voters, and a restarted ex-leader that kept an orphan suffix; other TrailingLogs, monotonic stores and larger clusters are not measured here.
Probe fields are read from the follower's cached state and its log store on the same process; the receipt is needed before treating the numbers as retained observations.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: in this revision a follower that accepts an InstallSnapshot whose index is not above its own cached last log index is left advertising a log it no longer holds and cannot accept any further log entry from that leader, so the cluster keeps re-shipping the same snapshot while the follower's applied state stays at the snapshot index. Basis, source side: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (src_install_snapshot_tail), getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry), the non-monotonic compaction path cannot remove a suffix that still lies above the snapshot index (src_compaction), every prev-log check then misses or mismatches so the leader only decrements nextIndex one step at a time (src_replicate_failure) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound and the leader re-sends the newest snapshot, after which nextIndex is reset to snapshotIndex+1 (src_send_snapshot_result). Basis, retained receipt (execution d1897256143f4de2b0477a3460ae392b, exit 0, both generated cases passed): in the trimmed case the setup event (index 0) recorded the victim's cached last log claim (index 95, term 2) with the leader's snapshot at index 83/term 3, its store 1-95 intact and zero restores; after reconnecting, the probe event (index 14) recorded the victim's FSM restored 4 -> 1193 times inside the 3s window with the leader's snapshot index still 83 (leader_snapshot_is_unchanged true), the victim's applied index unchanged at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95 with new entries committed and applied elsewhere, the cached claim still (index 95, term 2) with the store suffix 84-95 kept, the victim's commit index still 0, and exactly one stable leader set over the window. The untrimmed control on the same history (setup index 15, probe index 29) accepted no snapshot at all (restores 0, repeated_snapshot_installs false), repaired the claim with entries (index 95, term 3) and caught up (applied 83 -> 95, commit 95), which excludes the mere existence of the stale suffix as the cause. The five declared comparisons resolved unknown, not holds: the admission event ca_setup carried no tag field, so the trimmed_setup/untrimmed_setup alias conditions could not be evaluated and the admission could not be associated ('Missing operation admission fields or identity', 'Ambiguous prerequisite association; missing trimmed_setup.tag'); the successor experiment fixes exactly that field. The raw retained values therefore support the account, but the comparison-level verdict, and with it the formal conclusion, is still pending. Limits: three voters, in-memory log store with a file snapshot store, TrailingLogs=10, a restarted ex-leader whose orphan suffix came from applies it accepted while partitioned, a 3s idle-plus-steady-writes window, and a single induced full partition; the vote-side consequence of the stale claim (knowledge-1) never triggered because no election occurred, the monotonic-store variant deletes the suffix instead of keeping it and needs its own receipt, and nothing here measures whether the state persists beyond the window or whether a larger cluster with several trimmed voters could still repair the node.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control accepted no snapshot, repaired the stale suffix with ordinary log entries and reached the cluster frontier, so a stale log suffix by itself does not stall replication; the trimmed leader log plus the install path is the trigger.

The successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower never campaigned: the receipt shows one stable leader set over the whole window and the victim's term fixed at 3, so the starved state is stable rather than self-healing in this configuration.
The five declared comparisons are recorded as unknown because the admission event omitted the mode field the alias conditions test; no completed comparison verdict exists yet for this question.
limitations: Measured configuration only: three voters, InmemStore plus FileSnapshotStore, TrailingLogs=10 versus a large control, an idle cluster with one write per 250ms sample, and a 3s observation window.

scope.description: Two real three-voter cluster histories in one process: a leader is isolated and appends entries that never reach a quorum, is shut down, and the remaining voters elect a leader, commit further entries and take a snapshot; the isolated node is then restarted on its unchanged in-memory log store and reconnected. In the trimmed case the leader's log store is compacted to TrailingLogs=10 so it can only repair by shipping that snapshot; in the control TrailingLogs is large so entries alone can repair. Each case samples the victim's restores, applied index, commit index, cached last log entry, last snapshot and store range, plus the cluster frontier, for a 3s window with steady new writes.
assumptions: Fault model: no message loss inside the injected transport; the only induced event is a full transport partition of one voter plus its clean shutdown and restart on the same stores.

Reused facilities: MakeClusterCustom/MakeClusterOpts with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, MockFSM wrapped by a counting Restore, and the NewRaft restart pattern used by TestRaft_SnapshotRestore_Progress.
The victim's orphan suffix is produced by real Apply calls it accepted as leader while partitioned, and it is kept because the restarted node replays its real log store.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds a test file.

basis.prefix: The harness builds the cluster with MakeClusterCustom (counting FSM), commits 60 entries, partitions the leader with c.Partition, fires 60 applies on it so they are appended locally without a quorum, waits for it to step down, shuts it down with Shutdown().Error(), waits for one of the remaining voters to be the only stable leader, commits 20 further entries, forces Snapshot(), records the snapshot and the trimmed store range, restarts the victim with NewRaft on its original stores and a fresh InmemTransport, reconnects it to both other transports, emits ca_setup with the premise fields, waits until the victim's applied index reaches the snapshot index, then samples every 250ms for 3s while applying one entry per sample on whichever node is leader, and finally emits ca_probe with the raw values and derived booleans.

scope.description: One five-voter history in one process: forty entries are committed on all five voters, the current leader and one follower are partitioned together and the leader appends a further forty entries that reach only that follower, so the pair holds an uncommitted suffix while the other three voters elect a new leader, commit twenty entries and publish a snapshot at an index below the suffix end. After healing, both minority members install that snapshot and become phantom holders. The same RequestVote, built from the stale follower's real cached claim and carrying the leadership-transfer flag, is then delivered to the phantom holder and to a majority voter whose cached state matches its snapshot.
assumptions: Fault model: no message loss inside the injected transport; the induced events are one partition of two voters from three, one clean retention of the minority suffix, and one explicit snapshot on the majority leader.

The stale candidate's claim is real (the follower really stores and caches the suffix it received from the deposed leader); the single supplied element is that its RequestVote carries the leadership-transfer flag, which is how a transferred-to or stale-transfer target campaigns and is what removes the known-leader rejection so the log test is reached.

Requests are delivered through another node's in-process transport with bounded retries, because a node's own transport has no peer entry for itself; retries only repeat the same single request payload.
Reused facilities: MakeClusterCustom with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport and MockFSM.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds test code.
Automatic snapshotting is disabled so the published snapshot index is controlled by the explicit Snapshot() call.

basis.prefix: The harness elects a leader in a five-voter cluster, commits forty entries, partitions the leader with one follower, drives forty further applies on the deposed leader so the pair shares an uncommitted suffix, waits for the pair to stop leading, waits for one of the remaining three to be the only stable leader, commits twenty entries there and forces Snapshot(), then heals the partition and waits until both minority members have installed the snapshot (their last snapshot index becomes non-zero). It records the phantom claim, snapshot and applied indexes on the phantom holder and on the second minority member, the consistent voter's claim/snapshot/applied, the leader's snapshot, and the candidate's real claim, then builds one RequestVote with term = the consistent voter's current term + 1, last log index/term from the stale follower's cached claim and the transfer flag, and delivers it to the phantom holder and to the consistent voter, recording the responses and the derived booleans.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: in this revision, a follower that accepts a snapshot while its own cached log extends at or beyond the leader's snapshot index is left with an inconsistent log claim and never accepts another log entry from that leader. Basis: installSnapshot updates lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (raft.go 1930-1977), while getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (state.go 160-175). Compaction cannot remove the stale suffix in the non-monotonic store path when TrailingLogs exceeds the log length (snapshot.go 217-252), so the follower's store keeps entries above the snapshot index whose terms differ from the leader's; every AppendEntries prev-log check then either misses below the store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix, the leader's nextIndex is only decremented one step per rejection (replication.go 247-252) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, and the leader responds by re-shipping the same snapshot (replication.go 296-300, 352-372). Restricted to the measured conditions: three voters, in-memory store, FileSnapshotStore, TrailingLogs=10, an idle cluster plus steady new writes, and a follower restarted on its real on-disk log whose orphan suffix (indexes beyond the leader's snapshot index, lower term) is preserved. Local construction feedback for the same harness (native feedback only, not a retained receipt) showed the follower's FSM restored 4 -> 1365 times in a 3s window while the leader's snapshot index stayed at 83, the follower's applied index stayed at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95, the follower's cached last log claim stayed (98, term 2) against snapshot (83, term 3), its commit index stayed 0, and its store kept indexes 84-98; the untrimmed control on the identical history accepted no snapshot, repaired the suffix with entries and caught up (applied 83 -> 95). Counterevidence considered: the concern that the follower's own election timeout would repair the situation is not observed, because a successful InstallSnapshot refreshes lastContact, so no spurious election fires; and the control refutes 'any stale suffix stalls replication'. Limits: the formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained run of the requested experiment; the reachability of the trigger in production depends on a voter whose log suffix is both longer than the leader's snapshot index and stale in term (a deposed leader or a follower that stored entries from a superseded leader) together with log trimming on the leader; monotonic-store deployments delete the stale suffix instead of keeping it, so their failure mode (entry starvation with the leader's snapshot index at or below the cached claim) still needs its own receipt.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control with the same history repaired the stale suffix using log entries alone, so a stale suffix by itself is not sufficient; the install-snapshot path with a trimmed leader log is the trigger.
The successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower does not force an election and the starved state is stable rather than transient in the measured configuration.
limitations: The measured configuration used in-memory stores plus a file snapshot store, TrailingLogs=10, three voters, and a restarted ex-leader that kept an orphan suffix; other TrailingLogs, monotonic stores and larger clusters are not measured here.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: a follower that accepts an InstallSnapshot whose index does not exceed its own cached last log index keeps advertising a log it no longer holds, fails every prev-log check from that leader and accepts no further log entry, while the leader retries the same snapshot; the starvation ends only when a snapshot above the cached claim is published, and it reproduces at three and five voters. Source basis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (src_install_snapshot_tail); getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry, state.go 160-174); the non-monotonic compaction path keeps any suffix above the snapshot index while the monotonic branch deletes the whole store without resetting the claim (src_compaction, snapshot.go 217-279); prev-log verification then misses below the store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix (src_append_prev_check, raft.go 1458-1606); the leader walks nextIndex down one step per rejection (src_replicate_failure, replication.go 240-300) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, which jumps to SEND_SNAP and, on acceptance, resets nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1 (src_send_snapshot_result, replication.go 352-372). Decided evidence: the settled comparison set (execution b6089b103bbb467199d051f4492e82c8, trimmed probe index 14) with the untrimmed control negative on the same fields (index 29); the monotonic-store variant, where the store was emptied while the claim persisted (execution 20c7c72772474093bd6093a37b84448f, probe index 14); the repair boundary, where driving the leader past the claim of 97 and publishing a snapshot at 98 restored the follower to the frontier (same receipt, probe index 33); and the five-voter repetition (execution 14e86faf6ccc4b13af3ee46c65cc08dc, setup index 0 and probe index 14), where the premise recorded a claim at index 102 in term 2 over a snapshot at 83 in term 3 and the probe again showed repeated installs, the follower's applied index fixed while the frontier advanced, and the claim persisting with its suffix kept. Limits: measured on InmemStore plus FileSnapshotStore and its in-process monotonic wrapper with TrailingLogs=10 against a large control, an idle cluster with one write per 250 ms sample, 3-4 s windows and one induced partition, now repeated at three and five voters; a ten-second persistence run is requested with this update and is currently construction feedback (follower fixed at 83 while the frontier reached 123, restores 5 -> 4883, one stable leader set); the vote-decision consequence of the claim is decided in the child question, the configuration-change and wedge consequences likewise, and the follower's commit index staying 0 through the install path is reported as an advertised-state inconsistency rather than an independent defect.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control accepted no snapshot, repaired the stale suffix with entries and reached the frontier in every run, so a stale suffix alone does not stall replication.
A successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower never campaigned: every receipt shows one stable leader set with the follower's term fixed.

The starvation is bounded: with a snapshot published above the claim (97 -> 98) the follower caught up to the frontier, so the claim is starvation while the newest snapshot index stays at or below the claim.
The monotonic-store case stalls with an empty log store, so a surviving on-disk suffix is not required for the defect.
limitations: Store and snapshot implementations are the in-process ones (InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, the monotonic wrapper); a production BoltDB-style store is not available in the captured package.
Windows measured are 3-4 s, with a ten-second persistence run requested here; the frontier advance during a window is bounded by the one write per sample.

The configuration-change and vote consequences are decided in the child question and are not re-measured here; the child's minority bound assumes no configuration change between the orphaned suffix and the snapshot install.
